version.author: Thomas LeRoy Meier
version.changelog:
Two long-standing bugs, both present since the first release.
The IMA ADPCM codec never worked. Its index table shared a base address with the sample rate table, so changing any parameter overwrote part of it and pinned the decoder at its maximum step size. IMA has been producing permanent maximum-step distortion rather than IMA compression. It now decodes correctly, so this codec will sound substantially different - and correct - for the first time.
The filter and predictor states were initialised to their own array indices instead of zero, so the lo-fi filter started with a large impulse and the PSX feedback path started railed. These were only cleared when transport started, so a live-monitored or record-armed track never cleared them at all. All state is now zeroed when the effect loads.

version.author: Thomas LeRoy Meier
version.changelog:
The high-frequency damping in the feedback path never ran. Its filter state was being reset every single sample, which reduced the filter to a flat gain. Earlier release notes for this plugin claimed the damping fixed squealing at high feedback; that was not true, and is true now.
The output limiter ran after the delay buffer was written, so it protected the output but never the feedback loop. At high feedback with Dirt and Moonlight/Sunlight at zero the buffer could overflow to infinity, after which any tap set to zero volume produced NaN, which then spread through the buffer and silenced the plugin until it was reloaded. The loop is now bounded before the write, with a soft knee only above the limit, so normal levels are unchanged.
The Algorithm, Timing and Invert parameters are now range-checked. Out-of-range automation could read outside the algorithm table and be used as delay times.
Saved plugin state is now checked when a project loads. The state format is unchanged, so existing projects load exactly as before.

version.author: Thomas LeRoy Meier
version.changelog:
Feedback now tops out at 0.99 instead of 1.0. Exactly unity feedback is the condition that made the buildup in 7.3 possible. The 60%, 80% and 90% character thresholds are all still reachable, so the sound at high feedback is unchanged.
A project saved with feedback at 1.0 will load at 0.99.
